title: Pointwise convergence plus an eventual uniform Lipschitz bound on a compact set gives uniform convergence
statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, K ⊆ ℝⁿ (= Euclid n) compact, F_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) arbitrary functions, and a, L ∈ ℝ. Assume (i) F_k(x) → a as k → ∞ for every x ∈ K, and (ii) for all sufficiently large k, |F_k(x) − F_k(x')| ≤ L·dist(x, x') for all x, x' ∈ K. Then F_k converges to the constant function a uniformly on K.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (K : Set (Euclid n)) (F : ℕ → Euclid n → ℝ) (a L : ℝ), IsCompact K → (∀ x ∈ K, Tendsto (fun k => F k x) atTop (𝓝 a)) → (∀ᶠ k in atTop, ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ x' ∈ K, |F k x - F k x'| ≤ L * dist x x') → TendstoUniformlyOn F (fun _ => a) atTop K
